findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an `execFile` argument
findings.body: When `branch` is supplied by an untrusted caller, shell metacharacters are interpreted before Git validates the ref, allowing command execution with the application's privileges. For example, `git check-ref-format --branch` accepts a value containing `;printf${IFS}...`; interpolating that value into `exec()` executes the appended command. Keep Git as the executable and pass `branch` in the argument array.

findings.title: [P2] Keep Git as the directly cancellable child
findings.body: When a caller cancels a long-running `git show` through the returned `ChildProcess`, `exec()` targets the intermediary shell rather than Git. On POSIX, killing that shell does not reliably terminate its child, so Git can continue consuming CPU and I/O after cancellation. `execFile()` preserves direct process ownership and the prior cancellation behavior.
